description.value:
Denman Rooke

Barbarians are mighty warriors who are powered by primal forces of the multiverse that manifest as a Rage. More than a mere emotion—and not limited to anger—this Rage is an incarnation of a predator's ferocity, a storm's fury, and a sea's turmoil.

Some Barbarians personify their Rage as a fierce spirit or revered forebear. Others see it as a connection to the pain and anguish of the world, as an impersonal tangle of wild magic, or as an expression of their own deepest self. For every Barbarian, their Rage is a power that fuels not just battle prowess, but also uncanny reflexes and heightened senses.

Barbarians often serve as protectors and leaders in their communities. They charge headlong into danger so those under their protection don't have to. Their courage in the face of danger makes Barbarians perfectly suited for adventure.

Wayne England

Level 1: Rage

You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] if you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

You can enter your Rage the number of times shown for your Barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian Features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB], and you regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

While active, your Rage follows the rules below.

Damage Resistance. You have @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Rage Damage. When you make an attack using Strength—with either a weapon or an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB]—and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain levels as a Barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian Features table.

Strength Advantage. You have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

No Concentration or Spells. You can't maintain @status[Concentration|XPHB], and you can't cast spells.

Duration. The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition. If your Rage is still active on your next turn, you can extend the Rage for another round by doing one of the following:

  • Make an attack roll against an enemy.
  • Force an enemy to make a saving throw.
  • Take a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] to extend your Rage.

Each time the Rage is extended, it lasts until the end of your next turn. You can maintain a Rage for up to 10 minutes.

Level 1: Unarmored Defense

While you aren't wearing any armor, your base @variantrule[Armor Class|XPHB] equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Constitution modifiers. You can use a @item[Shield|XPHB] and still gain this benefit.

Level 1: Weapon Mastery

Your training with weapons allows you to use the @variantrule[weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties] of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice, such as @item[Greataxe|XPHB|Greataxes] and @item[Handaxe|XPHB|Handaxes]. Whenever you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Barbarian levels, you gain the ability to use the @variantrule[weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties] of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Barbarian Features table.

Level 2: Danger Sense

You gain an uncanny sense of when things aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge perils. You have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition.

Level 2: Reckless Attack

You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with increased ferocity. When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] during that time.

Level 3: Barbarian Subclass

You gain a Barbarian subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Barbarian levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Barbarian level or lower.

Level 3: Primal Knowledge

You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1.

In addition, while your Rage is active, you can channel primal power when you attempt certain tasks; whenever you make an ability check using one of the following skills, you can make it as a Strength check even if it normally uses a different ability: &Reference[skill=Acrobatics], &Reference[skill=Intimidation], &Reference[skill=Perception], &Reference[skill=Stealth], or &Reference[skill=Survival]. When you use this ability, your Strength represents primal power coursing through you, honing your agility, bearing, and senses.

Level 4: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the @feat[Ability Score Improvement|XPHB] feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Barbarian levels 8, 12, and 16.

Level 5: Extra Attack

You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the @action[Attack|XPHB] action on your turn.

Level 5: Fast Movement

Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

Level 6: Subclass Feature

You gain a feature from your Barbarian subclass.

Level 7: Feral Instinct

Your instincts are so honed that you have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on @variantrule[Initiative|XPHB] rolls.

Level 7: Instinctive Pounce

As part of the @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] you take to enter your Rage, you can move up to half your @variantrule[Speed|XPHB].

Level 8: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the @feat[Ability Score Improvement|XPHB] feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Level 9: Brutal Strike

If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn't have @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB]. If the chosen attack roll hits, the target takes an extra [[/damage 1d10]] damage of the same type dealt by the weapon or @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], and you can cause one Brutal Strike effect of your choice. You have the following effect options.

Forceful Blow. The target is pushed 15 feet straight away from you. You can then move up to half your @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] straight toward the target without provoking @action[Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks].

Hamstring Blow. The target's @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] is reduced by 15 feet until the start of your next turn. A target can be affected by only one Hamstring Blow at a time—the most recent one.

Level 10: Subclass Feature

You gain a feature from your Barbarian subclass.

Level 11: Relentless Rage

Your Rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] while your Rage is active and don't die outright, you can make a [[/save ability=con dc=10]] saving throw. If you succeed, your @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] instead change to a number equal to twice your Barbarian level.

Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], the DC resets to 10.

Level 12: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the @feat[Ability Score Improvement|XPHB] feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Level 13: Improved Brutal Strike

You have honed new ways to attack furiously. The following effects are now among your Brutal Strike options.

Staggering Blow. The target has @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] on the next saving throw it makes, and it can't make @action[Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks] until the start of your next turn.

Sundering Blow. Before the start of your next turn, the next attack roll made by another creature against the target gains a +5 bonus to the roll. An attack roll can gain only one Sundering Blow bonus.

Level 14: Subclass Feature

You gain a feature from your Barbarian subclass.

Level 15: Persistent Rage

When you roll @variantrule[Initiative|XPHB], you can regain all expended uses of Rage. After you regain uses of Rage in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

In addition, your Rage is so fierce that it now lasts for 10 minutes without you needing to do anything to extend it from round to round. Your Rage ends early if you have the &Reference[condition=Unconscious] condition (not just the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition) or don Heavy armor.

Level 16: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the @feat[Ability Score Improvement|XPHB] feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Level 17: Improved Brutal Strike

The extra damage of your Brutal Strike increases to [[/damage 2d10]]. In addition, you can use two different Brutal Strike effects whenever you use your Brutal Strike feature.

Level 18: Indomitable Might

If your total for a Strength check or Strength saving throw is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

Level 19: Epic Boon

You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. @feat[Boon of Irresistible Offense|XPHB] is recommended.

Level 20: Primal Champion

You embody primal power. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

Ona Kristensen

Path of the Fractured

Two Personalities Are Better than One

Barbarians are defined by their rage, channeling it to unleash brief but potent destruction. Few are brave or unwise enough to study esoteric psychological techniques that split their rage from the rest of their psyche, dividing their identity into two parts: ego and id. When their ego is in control, the Fractured—as these Barbarians are known—possess self-control and cunning beyond most other Barbarians. When they allow their id to take control, their countenance turns monstrous and their bodies swell with the power of rage made physically manifest.

Level 3: Face of Rage

When you activate your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1], your countenance distorts and your body swells. Creatures that haven't witnessed your transformation, now or previously, don't recognize you. In addition, while your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] is active, you gain the following benefits:

  • You can roll [[/r 1d8]] in place of the normal damage of your @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], and whenever you deal damage with an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.
  • When you hit a creature with an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], you can push it 10 feet or force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and your @variantrule[Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus]). On a failed save, the creature has the &Reference[condition=Prone] condition.
  • You count as one size larger when determining the success or failure of a Grapple, and when you make an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], your reach is 5 feet greater than normal.

Level 3: Mask of Civility

You are proficient in one of the following skills of your choice: &Reference[skill=Arcana], &Reference[skill=History], &Reference[skill=Investigation], &Reference[skill=Medicine], &Reference[skill=Nature], &Reference[skill=Persuasion], or &Reference[skill=Religion]. In addition, you gain proficiency with one type of @item[Artisan's Tools|XPHB] of your choice or you know one language of your choice.

Level 6: Brains and Brawn

While your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] is not active, you have @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to Psychic damage. While your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] is active, you have @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to every damage type except Force and Psychic.

Level 10: Cunning and Brutal

While your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] is not active, you can take the @action[Disengage|XPHB] or @action[Help|XPHB] action as a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB]. While your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] is active, your attack rolls with @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes] score a @variantrule[Critical Hit|XPHB] on a roll of 19 or 20 on the [[/r d20]].

Level 14: Better Half

When you are reduced to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] and not killed outright, you can drop to 1 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point] instead, and you gain @variantrule[Temporary Hit Points|XPHB] equal to half your @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point] maximum. In addition, if your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] is active, your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] ends. If your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] was not active, you immediately activate your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] (even if you have no remaining uses of your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1]). If any of these @variantrule[Temporary Hit Points|XPHB] remain after 1 minute, they vanish.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Humans are known for being ambitious, diverse, and extremely short-lived, but also have the dubious honor of being associated with an abundance of near-human offshoots, for it seems humans can breed with just about anything. Near-humans are still basically humans, bearing subtly different traits from a wide variety of sources, and are individually rare but make up a surprisingly large portion of any human population

Prerequisites: Near-Human, 1st level only Feature

Your coarse features and monstrous build betray that one of your parents is an ogre. You have the following racial traits:

Ability Score Increase. Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Darkvision. You can see in &Reference[rule=dimlight]{dim light} within 60 feet of you as if it were &Reference[rule=brightlight]{bright light}, and in darkness as if it were &Reference[rule=dimlight]{dim light}. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

Monstrous Strength. You gain proficiency in the &Reference[skill=Athletics] skill. Additionally, when you make a Strength (&Reference[skill=Athletics]) check, you can treat the result as a 10, or your level plus your Strength modifier, whichever is higher.

Powerful Build. You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

You are haunted by the events of your past. Whether it was a lone terrible incident or an accumulation of painful moments, you bear the unshakable weight of what happened to you. You've tried to bury it and run away from it, to no avail; it can't be slain with a sword or banished via magic. Nevertheless, you persist.

  • Ability Scores: Constitution, Wisdom, Charisma

  • Feat: @feat[Survivor|RHW] or a Dark Gift feat of your choice

  • Skill Proficiencies: &Reference[skill=Arcana] and &Reference[skill=Survival]

  • Tool Proficiencies: Choose one kind of @item[Gaming Set|XPHB]

  • Equipment: Choose A or B: (A) @item[Gaming Set|XPHB] (same as above), @item[Crowbar|XPHB], @item[Holy Water|XPHB] (1 @item[flask|XPHB]), @item[Mirror|XPHB], @item[Oil|XPHB](2 @item[flask|XPHB|flasks]), @item[Signal Whistle|XPHB], @item[Tinderbox|XPHB], @item[Traveler's Clothes|XPHB], 5 @item[Torch|XPHB|Torches], @item[Waterskin|XPHB], and 14 GP; or (B) 50 GP

description.value:
Potion, Uncommon

When you drink this potion, your Strength score changes for 1 hour to 21. The type of giant determines the score. The potion has no effect on you if your Strength is equal to or greater than that score.

This potion's transparent liquid has floating in it a sliver of light resembling a giant's fingernail.

Dark Gift Feat (Prerequisite: Ravenloft Campaign)

A second being resides within your body, offering knowledge and assistance while furthering its own agenda. You gain the following features.

Entwined Existence. The symbiote can't be targeted. If you die, so does your symbiote. If you are returned to life, your symbiote also revives.

Second Mind. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills: &Reference[skill=Arcana], &Reference[skill=Deception], &Reference[skill=History], &Reference[skill=Intimidation], &Reference[skill=Insight], &Reference[skill=Investigation], &Reference[skill=Nature], &Reference[skill=Religion], &Reference[skill=Perception], or &Reference[skill=Persuasion]. You also know one additional language of your choice, chosen from the language tables in the Player's Handbook.

Sustained Symbiosis. When you fail a saving throw, you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] and expend one of your Hit Dice. Roll the die and add the number rolled to the saving throw, potentially turning the failure into a success.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your @variantrule[Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus], and you regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Symbiotic Agenda. Immediately after you make a @variantrule[D20 Test|XPHB] and roll a 1 on the [[/r d20]], your symbiote attempts to assert control. Make a Charisma saving throw (DC 13 plus your @variantrule[Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus]). On a failed save, you have the &Reference[condition=Charmed] condition for [[/r 1d12]] hours. While &Reference[condition=Charmed], you must try to follow the symbiote's commands and further its goals, as determined by the DM. Whenever you take damage, you can repeat this save, ending the effect on a success.

At the DM's discretion, you might make this saving throw whenever you act contrary to the symbiote's agenda.

activation.condition: When you fail a saving throw

You are a skilled practitioner of the forge, capable of keeping gear in fighting shape, crafting reliable equipment, and applying temporary improvements to arms and armor. You gain the following benefits:

  • Basic Repair. During a short or long rest, you can use your Smith's Tools to repair one damaged nonmagical weapon, suit of armor, or shield, restoring its standard functionality.

  • Efficient Forging. When you use your Smith's Tools to craft a nonmagical weapon, suit of armor, or shield, the material cost required is reduced by 15% (or just DM consider).

  • Equipment Maintenance. During a long rest, you can spend time honing an edge or reinforcing plates on one nonmagical weapon or suit of armor using your Smith's Tools.

    • Weapon: Grants a +1 bonus to damage rolls on its next 3 successful hits.

    • Armor/Shield: Grants +1 AC against the first attack roll that hits you in the next combat encounter.

    This temporary improvement fades after your next long rest. You can maintain only one item in this way at a time.

This spell repairs a single break or tear in an object you touch, such as a broken chain link, two halves of a broken key, a torn cloak, or a leaking wineskin. As long as the break or tear is no larger than 1 foot in any dimension, you mend it, leaving no trace of the former damage.

This spell can physically repair a magic item, but it can't restore magic to such an object.

Granted by Forge Hammer

This potion is a magic item. As a Bonus Action, you can drink it or administer it to another creature within 5 feet of yourself. The creature that drinks the magical red fluid in this vial regains 2d4 + 2 Hit Points.

3rd Level &Reference[Spell Scroll]

You touch a creature that has died within the last minute. That creature revives with 1 Hit Point. This spell can't revive a creature that has died of old age, nor does it restore any missing body parts.
